title: The boy reading a book
goal: Describe people and things with -ýAn and -mAýAn before the noun.

intro.text: Turn a sentence into a phrase: *Oglan kitap okaýar* (the boy is reading a book) → *kitap okaýan oglan* (the boy who is reading a book). `-ýAr` becomes `-ýAn`, and the noun moves to the end. Not: `-mAýAn`, *çilim çekmeýän adam*.

exercises.question: Which phrase means **the boy who is reading a book**?

why.1: This is a full sentence: **the boy is reading a book**.
why.2: The noun comes last: *kitap okaýan oglan*.
why.3: `-ýAr` ends a sentence. Before a noun, use the participle: *okaýan*.

exercises.explain: *okaýar* → *okaýan*, and the noun goes to the end: *kitap okaýan oglan*.
As before *-ýär*, the t becomes d: *gidýän*.

exercises.en: I know the man who sells carpets at the bazaar.

reject.why: *-ýar* ends a sentence. Before a noun: *satýan adam*.

accept: The boy reading a book is my brother.
The boy who is reading a book is my brother.
The boy [reading|who is reading] the book is my brother.
The boy who reads books is my brother.

exercises.prompt: I know the woman who sells bread.

reject.why: Everything that describes the woman comes before her: *çörek satýan aýaly*.
*Satýar* ends a sentence. Before a noun: *satýan*.

exercises.explain: *çörek satýan aýal* (the woman who sells bread) + the accusative after *tanamak*: *aýaly*.

exercises.question: How do you say **people who don't smoke**?

why.1: *Çekmeýär* ends a sentence. Before a noun: *çekmeýän*.
why.2: The noun comes last: *çilim çekmeýän adamlar*.

accept: There are few tourists who speak Turkmen.
Tourists who speak Turkmen are few.
There are not many tourists who speak Turkmen.

exercises.prompt: My colleague who lives in Mary is coming tomorrow.

exercises.text: Hiç zat etme___ ýalta adamlary halamaýaryn.
exercises.en: I don't like lazy people who do nothing.

reject.why: *Etmeýär* ends a sentence. Before a noun: *etmeýän adamlar*.

exercises.explain: *et-* + *-me-* + *-ýän*; the adjective stays next to the noun: *hiç zat etmeýän ýalta adamlar*.

exercises.prompt: Who is the boy playing the dutar?

reject.why: The noun comes last: *dutar çalýan oglan*.
*Çalýar* ends a sentence. Before a noun: *çalýan*.

exercises.explain: *dutar çalýan oglan* (the boy playing the dutar) + *kim?*

exercises.question: *Işleýän adam* means…
options: a person who works or is working

why.1: That is *işlän adam*, with `-An`, in the next lesson.
why.2: That needs another participle, in [B1 unit 6](b1-u06).

exercises.explain: `-ýAn` is for what is going on or usual: *işleýän adam*.

accept: The woman who works in the library is very hard-working.
The woman who works at the library is very hard-working.
The woman working in the library is very hard-working.
The woman who works [in|at] the library is very [diligent|hardworking].
